issues.description: Part 1 directly reads 19 author-named .dta files from the [redacted-path-0cbd15600f04] JAR Replications tree. None of those files is in this package; the only packaged .dta is an individualid/CRD list, not a complete analysis input. The datasheet describes historical BrokerCheck scraping and Python parsing, but no scraper/parser is supplied. Locate compatible prepared inputs or a documented compatible route and verify fields/history; the old collection date alone does not establish observation coverage.

Part 1 writes Main Advisor Sample.dta and Main Advisory Firm Sample.dta, whereas Part 2 directly reads 12 separate Data for Table*.dta files, including the unlisted Data for Table 06, 07A, and 10A.dta. No supplied producer or handoff connects the Part 1 outputs to these table inputs, so the full table workflow order and schemas remain unknown. Keep source lineage conditional until the author bridge is identified: the datasheet reports ACS/Social Explorer for Census data and CRSP Mutual Fund/WRDS; catalog discovery did not verify a CRSP mutual-fund route, access, or entitlement. Table 8’s factor/portfolio source is also unspecified. Part 1’s regfirm_90, lnbusinesstypecount, and lnstatereg do not directly match Part 2’s highrisk_brokerage, lnnum_business_lines, and lnnum_state_reg; do not guess aliases.

The shared Table 06/07A/10A block uses settled_complaint in a regression and the shorter token settle in tabstat. The shorter token may be a valid unique Stata variable abbreviation. The table dataset and effective varabbrev setting are not available here, so this is not a confirmed field mismatch. Inspect the schema and active setting before execution; ask for clarification only if abbreviation is disabled, ambiguous, or intended to refer to a genuinely different field.

Both scripts use a coherent [redacted-path-0cbd15600f04] JAR Replications project root: Part 1 uses its advisor/firm subdirectories, and Part 2 uses that root for its table inputs and log. Mapping this known tree to the Linux run environment is supported path preparation and can be chosen independently of the unresolved table-data producer.

The invoked Stata commands gduplicates, gcollapse, gdistinct, and distinct were not found in the checked adopaths. StataCorp and the package repositories document SSC installation routes; install/configure the required command packages and verify the actual command entry points under Stata 18.

steps: Resolve or obtain the author-named advisor and firm .dta inputs listed by requirements R001–R019, or document a compatible author-prepared/source-derived route for each; do not treat the packaged CRD identifier list as the full sample.

review_notes: Scope is the two supplied March 8, 2019 Stata programs: Part 1 builds advisor and firm main samples; Part 2 claims the main Tables 1–10. No independent analysis-only scope is supported because the packaged CRD list is not a table-level analysis input and no compatible prepared table dataset route is verified.

The inventory lists only one packaged .dta, Identifiers for Final Sample.dta. Its bounded probe reads individualid (label crd), with file metadata count 1,041,643; this is an identifier list, not the analysis data needed by Part 2.

The exact Part 1 path aliases are 19 merge/read inputs; its only two saves are Main Advisor Sample.dta and Main Advisory Firm Sample.dta. Part 2 instead reads 12 Data for Table*.dta inputs. Treat the missing table-data bridge as unresolved, not as proof that the Part 1 samples are the Part 2 files.

The code itself creates advisor-year rows from begin/end and sets since to the earliest available year. Full employment-history coverage is unknown; the author’s 2017 scrape window is not an observation-history bound. Part 2 Table 1A loops 2007–2017 but also reports all-available-row totals.

The Table 05 ACS/Social Explorer and Table 09 CRSP Mutual Fund/WRDS references are source leads for the missing table-data producers. Catalog metadata does not verify CRSP mutual-fund coverage, access, or entitlement. A compatible route may use public/local sources and documented conversion/cleaning without requiring identical author bytes or an additional author-approval condition.

The datasheet and online appendix describe Google Trends and the Madoff-victim list for online-appendix investor-awareness tests. Those analyses are not read by either supplied entry program and remain conditional off-target leads, not mandatory inputs for this main Tables 1–10 scope.
The scripts are marked March 8, 2019 but do not declare a Stata version; available Stata 18 is not labeled incompatible on that basis. The four actually invoked user commands still need setup.
No author program, regression, dataset import beyond the provided one-row metadata probe, package installation, source edit, or download was performed. Execution remains unverified.

Part 2 calls newey on the Table 08 input without an explicit tsset/xtset line. The native .dta may carry time-series characteristics; inspect and preserve them, and clarify the intended time index only if none is present.
